newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BEVAN STRENGTHENS TEST CLAIMS WITH 150.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEVAN STRENGTHENS TEST CLAIMS WITH 150.

text.p: Michael Bevan made an unbeaten 150
on Sunday to reinforce his claim for a place in Australia's test
side to face West Indies as New South Wales took a stranglehold
on their Sheffield Shield match against Victoria.
Bevan was the cornerstone of his side's second innings total
of 353 for eight declared as New South Wales set Victoria a
target of 457 to win.
Victoria collapsed in their chase of the imposing target and
were 100 for five at the close of play on the third day with one
day remaining at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
Opener Matthew Elliott was the only Victorian batsman to
offer any resistance and was 63 not out.
Bevan is one of the candidates to fill the number three
position in the Australia side left vacant by David Boon's
retirement. The first test against West Indies starts in
Brisbane on November 22.
Bevan, who scored 79 in the first innings, was well
supported by Michael Slater, another test aspirant, with 69
after the failure of Australia captain Mark Taylor and
all-rounder Steve Waugh, who were both dismissed cheaply.
The stylish left-handed batsman was 58 overnight and scored
almost at will as he received valuable support from tail-end
batsmen Phil Emery and Anthony Stuart.
Victoria captain Shane Warne, who is battling to prove his
fitness for test duty after finger surgery in May, bowled 25
overs without reward to finish with none for 75.
Warne, Australia's main strike bowler with 207 wickets in 44
tests, took the wickets of two tail-enders in the New South
Wales first innings.
